title: account rename Command
description: Add an 'account rename' command that renames an existing account by any identifier (--name, --email, --zuidstring). The rename updates: AccountEntry.Name in accounts.json, the keychain credential entry key, and the accounts.json IsDefault flag if applicable. Validate that the new name does not collide with an existing account.
prerequisiteState: Stories 1–19 complete. ResolveAccountAsync exists. IAuthProvider has GetTokenAsync, StoreTokenAsync, RefreshTokenAsync, ClearTokenAsync. No rename operation exists anywhere.
goal: After this story: 'zapi-cli account rename --name old --new-name new' renames the account in all storage locations (accounts.json + keychain). The account is accessible by the new name immediately. The old keychain key is cleaned up.
scope: Add new error code to src/ZapiCli.Core/ErrorCodes.cs: public static readonly string ACCOUNT_RENAME_FAILED = "ACCOUNT_RENAME_FAILED"; with XML doc 'Thrown when the keychain credential rename operation fails (e.g., write succeeded but delete of old key failed).'

Add RenameTokenAsync(string oldName, string newName, CancellationToken ct = default) to src/ZapiCli.Core/Auth/IAuthProvider.cs. XML doc: 'Reads the credential bundle stored under oldName, writes it under newName, then deletes the oldName entry. If the write fails, throws ZapiCliException with KEYCHAIN_ERROR. If the delete fails after a successful write, throws with ACCOUNT_RENAME_FAILED (partial failure — the new key exists but the old key remains; the account is accessible by newName).'

Implement RenameTokenAsync in src/ZapiCli.Core/Auth/OAuthProvider.cs: (1) var json = await _keychain.GetAsync(MakeKey(oldName), ct); if null throw KEYCHAIN_ERROR ('No credentials found for account {oldName}'). (2) await _keychain.SetAsync(MakeKey(newName), json, ct); catch and throw KEYCHAIN_ERROR. (3) await _keychain.DeleteAsync(MakeKey(oldName), ct); catch exceptions and throw ACCOUNT_RENAME_FAILED with message 'Credentials written for {newName} but failed to remove old key {oldName}. Manually remove the old keychain entry if needed.'

Add RenameAccountAsync(string? name, string? email, string? zuidstring, string newName, CancellationToken ct = default) to src/ZapiCli.Core/Accounts/IAccountService.cs. XML doc: 'Renames an account identified by any one of name/email/zuidstring to newName. Updates accounts.json and the keychain key. Throws INVALID_ARGS if none or multiple identifiers provided. Throws ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND if no match. Throws ACCOUNT_ALREADY_EXISTS if newName is already taken. Throws KEYCHAIN_ERROR or ACCOUNT_RENAME_FAILED on keychain failure.'

Implement RenameAccountAsync in src/ZapiCli.Core/Accounts/AccountService.cs: (1) Validate newName: if null/whitespace throw INVALID_ARGS; if contains /\:*? throw INVALID_ARGS ('--new-name must not contain / \ : * ? characters.'). (2) ResolveAccountAsync to get existing entry (oldEntry). (3) Load AccountsRoot; check newName not already taken: if any existing account has Name == newName (StringComparison.Ordinal) throw ACCOUNT_ALREADY_EXISTS. (4) await _authProvider.RenameTokenAsync(oldEntry.Name, newName, ct). (5) Build updatedAccounts: replace oldEntry with oldEntry with { Name = newName } in the list. (6) await _accountStore.SaveAsync(new AccountsRoot { Accounts = updatedAccounts }, ct). (7) Return (oldEntry.Name, newName).

Add AccountRenameSettings and AccountRenameCommand to src/ZapiCli/Commands/AccountCommands.cs: Settings: [CommandOption("--name")] string? Name, [CommandOption("--email")] string? Email, [CommandOption("--zuidstring")] string? ZuidString, [CommandOption("--new-name <NEW_NAME>")] string? NewName. Validate(): exactly one source identifier; NewName is required; NewName must not contain /\:*? characters. ExecuteAsync: call _service.RenameAccountAsync(settings.Name, settings.Email, settings.ZuidString, settings.NewName!, ct). Output: { status: ok, data: { old_name: '...', new_name: '...' } }.
Register in src/ZapiCli/Program.cs: account.AddCommand<AccountRenameCommand>("rename").WithDescription("Rename an account and update its keychain entry.");

Unit tests in tests/ZapiCli.Tests/Accounts/AccountRenameTests.cs: (1) Rename by name — accounts.json updated, RenameTokenAsync called with correct old/new keys. (2) Rename by email — ResolveAccountAsync routes to FindByEmailAsync. (3) Rename to an existing name — throws ACCOUNT_ALREADY_EXISTS. (4) Rename with no source identifier — throws INVALID_ARGS. (5) Rename with multiple source identifiers — throws DUPLICATE_IDENTIFIER. (6) Rename with invalid characters in new-name — throws INVALID_ARGS. (7) Keychain write success but delete failure — throws ACCOUNT_RENAME_FAILED; accounts.json is already updated (tolerate partial keychain state).
acceptanceCriteria: IAuthProvider.RenameTokenAsync is declared and implemented in OAuthProvider
account rename command registered in Program.cs
Rename updates accounts.json and the keychain entry atomically-best-effort
All tests pass including new rename tests
contextForAgent: The keychain key format is 'zapi-cli:<accountName>:oauth'. MakeKey(name) in OAuthProvider returns $'zapi-cli:{name}:oauth'. RenameTokenAsync must call MakeKey on both oldName and newName. The partial failure scenario (write succeeded, delete failed) should not roll back the accounts.json write — the account is accessible by newName and the old keychain entry is orphaned but harmless. The error message for ACCOUNT_RENAME_FAILED must explicitly tell the user what happened so they can manually clean up the old keychain entry if desired.
